clue.text: Lions and tigers in Christ Church Meadows? In London rather

definitions.text: Lions and tigers in Christ Church Meadows? In London rather

parts.words: Lions and tigers in Christ Church Meadows? In London rather
parts.note: a big-top show with wild animals pitched in an Oxford college's meadows would be a circus in Oxford; the clue then points to the London road junction of that name instead

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a menagerie loose on the meadows of an Oxford college, then corrects themselves to a London location.
explanation.walkthrough: Christ Church is an Oxford college with famous meadows. OXFORD CIRCUS is a busy junction in London's West End, so the second sentence turns the Oxford circus into the London place.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a famous road junction and Underground station in central London, read literally as a menagerie show held in Oxford.

clue.text: An order to make the party stag beats this

definitions.text: An order to make the party stag
definitions.meaning: a stag party is men only, so the female deer are ordered out

explanation.surface: A command that turns a mixed party into a men-only one beats this one.
explanation.walkthrough: Does are female deer; 'does out!' would leave only stags. Read as a verb the word means surpasses.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat someone is to do better than them, to surpass their performance.

clue.text: They are handy, and tasty, if fishy

explanation.surface: Something useful and delicious, though somewhat suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: The digits are parts of the hand, and fish ones are a breaded frozen food.

clue.text: Going back to take in about two shillings

indicators.note: the verb is placed about, surrounding, the coins

parts.note: to receive is to take in, as goods or guests
S was the abbreviation for an old British shilling, so two of them are SS

explanation.surface: Someone retreating to collect a small sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated S.
explanation.definitionFit: Recessive means receding or tending to go back.

clue.text: Sound appeal by shaggy dogs, or by Milton

annotationWithheld.why: Sound appeal by shaggy dogs, or by Milton (5): Milton's masque is the definition, but no reading of 'Sound appeal by shaggy dogs' giving these letters could be found
annotationWithheld.clue: Sound appeal by shaggy dogs, or by Milton

clue.text: Freeing Lorna's John in Gateshead

parts.note: John Ridd is the hero who loves Lorna in Blackmore's novel Lorna Doone
read as 'Gate's head', the first letter of gate

explanation.surface: A romantic hero sets someone free in a town in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England; split as Gate's head it gives G.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridding is clearing or releasing from something unwanted, as freeing does.

clue.text: Supporter at The Queen's Arms tosses coin into a vessel

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go into the vessel

parts.note: an urn is a vase-like vessel

indicators.note: tossing throws the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker at a pub called The Queen's Arms throws a coin into a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tosses' rearranges COIN into NICO, put 'into' URN. The royal arms are held by a lion and this beast; the surface suggests a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The heraldic beast standing beside the lion on the British royal coat of arms is a supporter.

clue.text: Compass directions to give Cinderella a smooth ride in her coach?

definitions.text: Compass directions to give Cinderella a smooth ride in her coach?

parts.words: Compass directions to give Cinderella a smooth ride in her coach?
parts.note: compass directions are bearings, and Cinderella's coach takes her to the ball; the steel spheres in wheel hubs make the ride smooth

explanation.surface: Instructions for a fairy-tale coach to carry Cinderella comfortably.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardened steel balls in a race let wheels turn smoothly, and the word splits as dance plus compass headings.

clue.text: This Ray finds not quite nice after start of play

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for the adjective in the phrase 'actinic ray'

parts.note: the first act of a play is Act I, the point where it starts

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A man called Ray finds things less than pleasant once the play begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the final E of NICE, leaving NIC. Actinic rays are light rays able to cause chemical change, so 'This Ray' is the ray described by the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Actinic describes light radiation, such as ultraviolet, that produces photochemical effects, so it names a kind of ray.

clue.text: Bodily destination of a Berber's breakfast ?

definitions.text: Bodily destination of a Berber's breakfast ?

parts.words: Bodily destination of a Berber's breakfast ?
parts.note: a Riff is a Berber of the Rif mountains of Morocco, and his breakfast goes into the middle of him: the middle of a Riff

explanation.surface: A question about where a North African tribesman's morning meal ends up in the body.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riffs are a Berber people of northern Morocco; food eaten by a Riff ends up in his middle, so the body part is read as MID-RIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: The diaphragm region between chest and stomach is where food heads, and the word splits as middle plus Riff tribesman.

clue.text: Finnish at top of table? Sound idea, but two other languages made it

parts.note: French is one language
Polish is the second

explanation.surface: A diner from Finland at the head of a table hears a good idea built from two other tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finnish' sounds like finish, as 'Sound idea' says: a finish on a table top. The two languages are French and Polish.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy shellac coating gives furniture its surface finish.

clue.text: Freeborn heroine

parts.note: the heroine of Joy Adamson's book Born Free was Elsa, a female big cat raised by humans and returned to the wild

explanation.definitionFit: Elsa, the star of Born Free, was a female lion, so the heroine of that story is this animal.

clue.text: Thorny problem-what to do with one's little eyes (squinting slightly)?

indicators.note: a slight squint bends the sound a little, so the spoken phrase is close to, not exactly, the word entered

parts.words: what to do with one's little eyes
parts.note: with eyes crossed in a squint you can spy your own nose

explanation.surface: A tricky puzzle about what a child should do with their little eyes when they squint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thorny' is the definition, 'problem' a link. Squinting, one's little eyes spy (the) nose, and 'spy nose' said with a slight squint gives SPINOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinose is a botanical word for covered in spines, which is what a thorny stem is.

clue.text: Slackens and after a century stops completely

indicators.note: after the century is gone, the word that remains is what is left of it

parts.note: to cease is to come to a complete stop
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: A batsman eases off and stops scoring altogether once he has made a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' a century has gone, CEASES loses its C. The surface is cricket, where a batsman's century is a score of a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease something is to loosen or relax it, as slackening a rope does.

clue.text: In love and racing madly about-what chemistry is that '?

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, written as O

indicators.note: racing about madly, the letters of the word are thrown around into a new order

explanation.surface: A pair in love dash about wildly, wondering what sort of chemistry they share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly about' rearranges RACING into RGANIC, which follows IN and O. The chemistry of the surface is romantic; the definition wants the branch of the science.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry divides into organic and its counterpart, which studies compounds not based on carbon chains.

clue.text: Excursion in which 54 are surviving

indicators.note: the number goes in which, inside the trip

parts.note: an outing is a trip out
LIV is 54 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: On a trip, dozens of people manage to stay alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Outliving someone is living longer than them, surviving them.

clue.text: Coming up again the matter appears pressing

parts.note: res is Latin for thing or matter, as in res judicata
a pressing need is an urgent one

explanation.surface: A news item that keeps resurfacing seems to need attention badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resurgent is rising again after a decline, coming back up.

clue.text: This owl just doesn't give a hoot

definitions.text: This owl just doesn't give a hoot

parts.words: This owl just doesn't give a hoot
parts.note: a kind of owl known for its harsh shriek rather than a hoot; 'not give a hoot' also means not caring

explanation.surface: An owl that could not care less.
explanation.definitionFit: This species of owl makes a shrill cry rather than hooting, as its name says.

clue.text: Old boys' get-together is enough to ruin one

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are enough to make the answer when rearranged

explanation.surface: A gathering of former schoolmates is enough to wreck anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: RUIN ONE rearranges into the answer; 'is enough to' marks the letters as sufficient for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Old boys are former pupils of a school, and their gathering after years apart is a coming together again.

clue.text: Blast ! So much for my ace !

definitions.meaning: an old word for a trumpet call
a card player's lament when a top card is beaten by a card of the winning suit

explanation.surface: A bridge player curses as their best card is beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The word once meant a trumpet's blast, and at cards a card of the master suit beats even an ace.

clue.text: Painter all square with Marco ?

parts.note: a game left all square is a tie
Marco Polo, the Venetian traveller

explanation.surface: An artist level with an Italian named Marco.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiepolo was an 18th-century Venetian painter, and Marco Polo a Venetian traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was a Venetian artist famed for ceiling frescoes.

clue.text: Did its discovery beget that of titanium ?

definitions.text: Did its discovery beget that of titanium ?

parts.words: Did its discovery beget that of titanium ?
parts.note: Klaproth named one element after the planet Uranus and later named titanium after the Titans, children of Uranus in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A question of whether finding one element led to finding another.
explanation.definitionFit: This element, named after Uranus, is 'parent' to titanium, named after the Titans whom Uranus fathered.

clue.text: Run true to upbringing

indicators.note: the letters of the first words are turned to the answer, 'to' marking the change

explanation.surface: Someone stays faithful to the way they were raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' here means 'change into': RUN TRUE is rearranged into the answer, an old-fashioned anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The care and training given to a child as it grows up is its rearing.

clue.text: Tree issue worried Zola

indicators.note: worried letters are worked over into a new order

parts.note: the French novelist was Emile Zola

explanation.surface: A matter about trees troubles the French novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Zola's first name Emile, 'worried', is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin that oozes from certain tropical trees, a tree's exudation.

clue.text: Climbing hazard demonstrated by Mr. Winkle on the pond

definitions.meaning: a frozen cascade on a glacier, dangerous to mountaineers
in Dickens's Pickwick Papers Mr Winkle skates badly and tumbles on the frozen pond

explanation.surface: A mountaineering danger illustrated by a clumsy Dickens character skating.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated word read as two words describes what happens to Mr Winkle on ice.
explanation.definitionFit: On a glacier this is a steep frozen cascade; on a pond it is a tumble onto frozen water.

clue.text: "the earth, seems to me a —— promontory" (Hamlet)

definitions.text: "the earth, seems to me a —— promontory" (Hamlet)

parts.words: "the earth, seems to me a —— promontory" (Hamlet)
parts.note: Hamlet tells Rosencrantz and Guildenstern that this goodly frame the earth seems to him a barren headland; the blank wants that adjective

explanation.definitionFit: The word Shakespeare uses means barren, unable to produce life, fitting Hamlet's bleak view of the world.

clue.text: One egghead, fettered — one of these quirks of fate?

annotationWithheld.why: One egghead, fettered — one of these quirks of fate? : the only parse is I + E inside IRONS, where 'fettered' gives both the IRONS and the containment (in irons), one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: One egghead, fettered — one of these quirks of fate?

clue.text: Interior decorating job in the athletic club ?

definitions.text: Interior decorating job in the athletic club ?

parts.words: Interior decorating job in the athletic club ?
parts.note: redecorating alters a room; at a sports club the room where members alter their clothes has the same name

explanation.surface: A decorator is hired to do up a room at a sports club.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is the act of altering a room; at a club it is where athletes change clothes.
